# Templates

Built-in agent templates, copied into a project with `ragkit add agent <template>`. The copy is yours to edit.

| Template | Pattern | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`extractor`](#extractor) | `react` | Extracts structured fields (an invoice by default) from text into validated JSON. |
| [`knowledge-agent`](#knowledge-agent) | `react` | Researches your documents with repeated searches; good for multi-step questions. |
| [`rag-chat`](#rag-chat) | `rag-chat` | Answers questions from your documents with numbered citations (single-pass RAG). |
| [`sql-analyst`](#sql-analyst) | `react` | Answers data questions by exploring the schema and running read-only SQL. |
| [`supervisor`](#supervisor) | `supervisor` | Routes questions to a documents specialist and a data analyst, then combines their answers. |
| [`support-agent`](#support-agent) | `react` | Customer support agent that looks up order status and issues refunds with human approval. |

## `extractor` {#extractor}

Turns unstructured text into a validated object. The shape is a Pydantic model
in `schema.py` (an `Invoice` by default), named by `output_schema` in
`agent.yaml`. The result is validated against the model before it is returned.

```bash
ragkit chat extractor "INVOICE #A-1043 from Acme GmbH ... Total due: 95.20 EUR"
```

Over HTTP, `POST /agents/extractor/chat` returns the object in `structured`.

To extract something else, replace the models in `schema.py`, point
`output_schema` at your top-level model, and describe each field: the
descriptions are what the model reads.

Files: `agent.yaml`, `evals/golden.jsonl`, `prompts/system.md`, `schema.py`

??? example "agent.yaml"

    ```yaml
    # Extractor: turns unstructured text into a validated JSON object.
    # The structure is the Pydantic model named by output_schema; edit schema.py.
    name: extractor
    description: Extracts structured fields (an invoice by default) from text into validated JSON.
    pattern: react

    system_prompt: prompts/system.md
    output_schema: schema.py:Invoice

    memory:
      checkpointer: memory

    budget:
      max_steps: 3

    evals:
      dataset: evals/golden.jsonl
    ```

## `knowledge-agent` {#knowledge-agent}

Agentic retrieval: the model gets a `search_knowledge` tool and decides what to
search for, how many times, and when it has enough to answer. Use it for
comparisons and multi-step questions. It costs more model calls than
`rag-chat`; `budget.max_steps` caps them.

You can add your own tools in a `tools.py` and list them under `tools.local`
next to retrieval.

```bash
ragkit ingest docs
ragkit chat knowledge-agent "Compare the Pro and Team plans' storage limits"
```

Files: `agent.yaml`, `evals/golden.jsonl`, `prompts/system.md`

??? example "agent.yaml"

    ```yaml
    # Knowledge agent: researches your documents with a search tool.
    # The model decides what to search for and can search several times (agentic retrieval).
    name: knowledge-agent
    description: Researches your documents with repeated searches; good for multi-step questions.
    pattern: react

    system_prompt: prompts/system.md

    retrieval:
      collections: [docs]   # collections defined in ragkit.yaml
      mode: hybrid
      top_k: 5
      candidates: 50

    memory:
      checkpointer: memory

    budget:
      max_steps: 8          # caps the number of searches plus the final answer

    evals:
      dataset: evals/golden.jsonl
    ```

## `rag-chat` {#rag-chat}

Single-pass RAG: for every user message the agent searches the configured
collections once, puts the best passages in its prompt, and answers with
numbered citations. It makes one model call per message, so it is the
cheapest and fastest way to answer questions about your documents.

Use `knowledge-agent` instead when questions need several searches (comparisons,
multi-step questions).

| File | What to change |
|---|---|
| `agent.yaml` | `retrieval.collections` must name collections in `ragkit.yaml`; tune `top_k` and reranking |
| `prompts/system.md` | Answer style and citation rules |
| `evals/golden.jsonl` | Real questions and expected answers for `ragkit eval` (coming in M3) |

```bash
ragkit ingest docs
ragkit chat rag-chat "How do I reset my password?"
```

Files: `agent.yaml`, `evals/golden.jsonl`, `prompts/system.md`

??? example "agent.yaml"

    ```yaml
    # RAG chat: answers questions from your documents with citations.
    # Retrieves once per message and answers in a single model call (fast and cheap).
    name: rag-chat
    description: Answers questions from your documents with numbered citations (single-pass RAG).
    pattern: rag-chat

    system_prompt: prompts/system.md

    retrieval:
      collections: [docs]   # collections defined in ragkit.yaml
      mode: hybrid          # dense | sparse | hybrid
      top_k: 6              # passages given to the model
      candidates: 50        # results fetched before reranking
      # rerank: { provider: cohere }   # overrides the project's reranker

    memory:
      checkpointer: memory

    budget:
      max_steps: 2

    evals:
      dataset: evals/golden.jsonl
    ```

## `sql-analyst` {#sql-analyst}

Answers questions about a SQL database. It lists tables, inspects their
columns and sample rows, writes a SELECT, and explains the result with the SQL
it used.

Setup:

```bash
uv add "ragkit-agents[sql]" psycopg          # plus the driver for your database
export SQL_ANALYST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg://readonly:pass@host/db
ragkit chat sql-analyst "Which five customers spent the most this year?"
```

Safety: `run_query` accepts a single SELECT (or WITH) statement, rejects write
keywords, runs in a read-only transaction on Postgres and SQLite, enforces a
15-second statement timeout on Postgres, returns at most 200 rows, and always
rolls back. Treat these checks as a backstop and connect with a database user
that can only read.

| File | What to change |
|---|---|
| `tools.py` | Row limits, timeouts, or a different connection setting |
| `prompts/system.md` | Business definitions ("active customer means...") and naming conventions |

Files: `agent.yaml`, `evals/golden.jsonl`, `prompts/system.md`, `tools.py`

??? example "agent.yaml"

    ```yaml
    # SQL analyst: answers questions about a database by writing read-only SQL.
    # Set SQL_ANALYST_DATABASE_URL (SQLAlchemy URL) and use a read-only database user.
    name: sql-analyst
    description: Answers data questions by exploring the schema and running read-only SQL.
    pattern: react

    system_prompt: prompts/system.md

    tools:
      local: [list_tables, describe_table, run_query]

    memory:
      checkpointer: memory

    budget:
      max_steps: 10

    evals:
      dataset: evals/golden.jsonl
    ```

## `supervisor` {#supervisor}

A multi-agent coordinator. Each agent listed under `subagents` becomes an
`ask_<name>` tool; the supervisor decides whom to ask, sends each a
self-contained task, and merges the answers.

```bash
ragkit add agent knowledge-agent
ragkit add agent sql-analyst
ragkit add agent supervisor
ragkit chat supervisor "Which plan has SSO, and how many Team-plan customers signed up last month?"
```

How it behaves:

- Each sub-agent keeps its own memory per conversation (thread `<thread>/<agent>`), so
  follow-up delegations have context.
- Only the supervisor's own reply is streamed; sub-agent output reaches it as tool results.
- Supervisors can delegate to other supervisors; cycles are rejected at start-up.
- Agents that need human approval (`hitl`) cannot be sub-agents yet; start-up fails with
  a clear error if one is listed.

Files: `agent.yaml`, `evals/golden.jsonl`, `prompts/system.md`

??? example "agent.yaml"

    ```yaml
    # Supervisor: routes each request to specialist agents and combines their answers.
    # Every name under subagents must be an agent in this project; add them first, e.g.
    #   ragkit add agent knowledge-agent && ragkit add agent sql-analyst
    # Agents that need human approval (hitl) cannot be sub-agents yet.
    name: supervisor
    description: Routes questions to a documents specialist and a data analyst, then combines their answers.
    pattern: supervisor

    system_prompt: prompts/system.md

    subagents: [knowledge-agent, sql-analyst]

    memory:
      checkpointer: memory

    budget:
      max_steps: 8

    evals:
      dataset: evals/golden.jsonl
    ```

## `support-agent` {#support-agent}

A tool-using support agent (ReAct pattern). It answers questions and calls
`lookup_order` when it needs an order's status.

| File | What to change |
|---|---|
| `agent.yaml` | Model, tools, memory, step budget |
| `prompts/system.md` | Tone and rules |
| `tools.py` | Replace `lookup_order` with calls to your real systems; add more tools and list them under `tools.local` |
| `evals/golden.jsonl` | Questions and expected behaviour, used by `ragkit eval` (coming in M3) |

Try it:

```bash
ragkit chat support-agent "Where is order 1042?"
```

Files: `agent.yaml`, `evals/golden.jsonl`, `prompts/system.md`, `tools.py`

??? example "agent.yaml"

    ```yaml
    # Support agent: answers customer questions, looks up orders and issues refunds.
    name: support-agent
    description: Customer support agent that looks up order status and issues refunds with human approval.
    pattern: react

    # Leave unset to use default_model from ragkit.yaml.
    # model: google_genai:gemini-3.5-flash-lite
    # fallback_models: [openai:gpt-5.5]

    system_prompt: prompts/system.md

    tools:
      local: [lookup_order, issue_refund]
      # mcp:                       # tools from servers under mcp_servers in ragkit.yaml
      #   - server: tickets
      #     allow: [create_ticket]

    hitl:
      require_approval: [issue_refund]   # pauses until a person approves, edits or rejects
      decisions: [approve, edit, reject]

    memory:
      checkpointer: memory  # use postgres when running more than one server process

    budget:
      max_steps: 8

    evals:
      dataset: evals/golden.jsonl
    ```
